name: עַמִּישַׁדָּי
summary: A man of Dan in the wilderness, known only as the father of Ahiezer, the prince of Dan at the numbering, at the offering of the altar, and when Dan’s standard set out as the rear guard of all the camps (Num 1:12; 2:25; 7:66, 71; 10:25). It is עַם “kinsman, people” with the ־ִי of “my”, and שַׁדַּי, the name in which God appeared to the fathers (Gen 17:1; Exo 6:3): “my kinsman is Shaddai”. The same lists name the Danite spy עַמִּיאֵל, “my kinsman is God” (Num 13:12), and the other Shaddai names of the princes’ fathers, Zurishaddai and Shedeur.

evidence.note: “The standard of the camp of the sons of Dan set out, the rear guard of all the camps, and over its host Ahiezer son of עַמִּישַׁדָּי.”
Dan camping on the north, its prince Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai brings Dan’s offering on the tenth day (and 7:71).
“I am אֵל שַׁדַּי; walk before me and be whole”: the name the second element carries.
He appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as אֵל שַׁדַּי.
For the tribe of Dan, עַמִּיאֵל: the same pattern with אֵל.
Shelumiel son of צוּרִישַׁדָּי, “my rock is Shaddai”, in the same list.

note: The first element is עַם (entry am), whose sense “kinsman” for names in עַמִּי־ is argued there; the name is linked to this entry for its divine element, as Ammihud is linked to hod. Whether the ־ִי is “my” or a joining vowel (“kinsman of Shaddai”) the text does not settle. The name occurs at Num 1:12; 2:25; 7:66, 71; 10:25.
